title: Wastebasket Emoji 🗑️ Meaning: Trash Takes and Deleting
description: The 🗑️ wastebasket emoji means trash: something to delete or throw out, or an opinion, movie or team that's garbage. See slang uses, examples and combos.
summary: The 🗑️ wastebasket emoji shows an office trash can. Literally it means throwing something away or deleting a file. As slang it calls something “trash”: a bad take, a terrible movie, a losing team, an ex. People also aim it at themselves in self-deprecating jokes.
meaning: “Trash” is one of the internet's favorite verdicts, and 🗑️ delivers it in a single character. Replying with the bin to an opinion says it belongs in the garbage. Sports fans use it on rival teams and on their own after a bad loss. Reviews of films, albums and games use it as a rating. It is blunt and dismissive, with none of the playfulness of a clown or skull.

Turned inward, the insult becomes a joke. “I am 🗑️” or “trash for this show” borrows the fandom habit of calling yourself garbage for loving something a little too much. Someone who stayed up all night rewatching a series, or who went back to a habit they swore off, will describe themselves with the bin. It reads as cheerful self-mockery, not real distress.

The software meaning is the oldest. Computers have used a trash can or recycle bin icon for deleted files since the early days of graphical desktops, and apps still mark their delete button with one. So 🗑️ in a work chat usually means “remove this,” “scrap that draft” or “ignore my last message.” Reacting to your own mistaken post with it signals that you are retracting it.

Literal garbage talk accounts for the rest: bin day reminders, decluttering sprees, litter cleanups, kitchen chores. Breakup talk borrows the image too. “Took out the 🗑️” after ending things with someone is a well-worn line, and friends tend to answer it with applause. The same phrasing covers quitting a bad job, unfollowing an account or finally clearing out a storage unit.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Quote-posting a claim with 🗑️ rejects it outright. Rankings and tier lists place disliked items in a “trash” tier marked with it. In fandoms, people proudly label themselves trash for a character or pairing. The word “take” often sits next to it: “🗑️ take.”

contexts.label: In sports and gaming
contexts.body: Trash talk is practically what it was made for. Fans post it at opponents, referees and underperforming players. Gamers describe a weak weapon, a bad teammate or their own aim as 🗑️. Between friends it is banter; aimed at strangers it is simply an insult.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Here it nearly always means delete. “Old version can go 🗑️” or a bin reaction on an outdated file is clear and neutral. Using it on a colleague's idea is another matter and will be read as contempt, so keep it for things, not for people's contributions.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Household reminders, cleaning sprees and wardrobe purges take it literally. Friends also use it for verdicts on dates and exes, and for self-roasting after questionable decisions. Tone depends on the target: yourself is funny, the person you are texting less so.

examples.meaning: A fan disgusted with their team's performance.

examples.text: I'm 🗑️ for this couple, I've watched the finale four times
examples.meaning: Admitting to being embarrassingly obsessed with a show.

examples.text: Ignore the last file, wrong version 🗑️
examples.meaning: Asking colleagues to discard something sent in error.

examples.text: Blocked his number. Took out the 🗑️
examples.meaning: Describing ending contact with an ex as throwing away garbage.

combos.meaning: Throw it away; this belongs in the bin.
Trash goblin humor: gleefully identifying with a raccoon in the garbage.
Scrapping a draft or deleting a document.

confusedWith.difference: The 🚮 litter in bin sign is a public notice showing a figure dropping rubbish in a bin. It asks people to dispose of waste properly, and online it is also used to tell someone to throw a thing, or themselves, away.
The ♻️ recycling symbol is about reuse and sustainability, and online about reposting or recycled content. 🗑️ is about discarding for good.
The 💩 pile of poo also rates something as bad but is sillier and friendlier. The wastebasket is drier and more contemptuous.

avoid: Don't react with 🗑️ to a coworker's proposal; it reads as calling their work garbage.
Avoid calling a person 🗑️ in an argument unless you intend a real insult, since it attacks them and not their point.
design: The emoji is an open-topped office wastebasket, usually drawn as a gray or silver wire-mesh bin with a slight taper. Some platforms show a solid metal or plastic can, and a few have included crumpled paper inside. It is distinct from a lidded outdoor garbage can, which the emoji set does not include.

faqs.a: “Trash,” meaning worthless or awful. It is used on opinions, performances, products and people. Applied to oneself, it is a humorous confession of bad taste or weak willpower.
It is fandom-style language for being helplessly devoted to someone or something. The speaker is calling themselves trash in an affectionate, exaggerated way, not expressing low self-esteem.

faqs.q: What does 🗑️ mean in a work chat?
faqs.a: Delete or disregard. People use it to retract a message, mark a file as obsolete or agree that a plan should be dropped. It is neutral when aimed at objects.
It can be. Directed at someone's opinion or effort it is a harsh dismissal. For chores, file cleanup or jokes about yourself, it is harmless.
It became available in 2014 with Emoji 0.7. The litter in bin sign and the recycling symbol are older and were already on phones by then.
